title_en: BNY’s Slavin on Who’s Driving Active ETF Growth
title_zh: BNY 的 Ben Slavin 谈谁在驱动主动 ETF 增长
subtitle_zh: BNY ETF 主管 Slavin 拆解主动 ETF 资金流：谁在买、买什么。
description: BNY’s Slavin on Who’s Driving Active ETF Growth

turns.en: Welcome to Inside Active, a podcast about active managers that goes beyond soundbites and headlines and looks deeper into their processes, challenges, and philosophies in security selection. I'm David Cohn. I lead mutual fund and active research at Bloomberg Intelligence. Today, my co-host is Sharun Francis, Senior Associate Analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence. Sharun, thanks for joining me today.
turns.zh: 欢迎收听 Inside Active，这是一档关于主动管理型基金经理的播客，我们不满足于金句和头条，而是更深入地去看他们在证券选择上的流程、挑战和理念。我是 David Cohn，负责 Bloomberg Intelligence 的共同基金与主动管理研究。今天和我搭档主持的是 Sharun Francis，Bloomberg Intelligence 的高级副分析师（Senior Associate Analyst）。Sharun，感谢你今天来。

turns.en: Thanks for having me, David.
turns.zh: 谢谢你邀请我，David。

turns.en: So active ETFs have become one of the biggest growth stories in asset management. New products are launching at a rapid pace. Assets continue to climb and investors are putting billions of dollars into strategies that fall under the active ETF umbrella. But those headline numbers don't necessarily tell us what's driving the growth. Active ETFs now encompass everything from traditional stock and bond selection to systematic strategies, options income, and other approaches. And an investor buying an active ETF isn't necessarily making the same decision as an investor choosing an active mutual fund. They could be choosing active management, ETF wrapper, or some combination of the two. So to really understand the growth of active ETFs, we need to look beneath the aggregate flows. Who's actually buying them? What types of strategies they're buying? And what can tell us about the demand for active management? So joining us to discuss that is Ben Slavin, Global Head of ETFs at BNY. Ben, thanks for joining us.
turns.zh: 主动 ETF（active ETF）已经成为资产管理行业最大的增长故事之一。新产品以极快的速度发行，资产规模持续攀升，投资者正把数十亿美元投入各种归在主动 ETF 名下的策略。但这些表面上的总量数字，未必能告诉我们增长到底是由什么驱动的。如今的主动 ETF 涵盖了从传统的股票和债券选股，到系统化策略、期权收益（options income）以及其他各种方法。而且一个买主动 ETF 的投资者，做的决定未必和买主动共同基金的投资者一样。他可能是在选择主动管理、选择 ETF 这个外壳（wrapper），或者两者的某种组合。所以要真正理解主动 ETF 的增长，我们得往总量资金流的下面看：到底是谁在买？他们买的是哪些类型的策略？这些又能告诉我们关于主动管理需求的什么信息？今天来和我们聊这个话题的，是 BNY 的全球 ETF 主管 Ben Slavin。Ben，感谢你加入我们。

turns.en: Great. Thanks for having me, David.
turns.zh: 太好了。谢谢你邀请我，David。

turns.en: So, you know, as David mentioned, active ETFs have emerged as one of the fastest growing segments of the ETF industry. You know, launches have accelerated and they even outnumber passive products now. But before we get into who's buying them, what does BNY's data tell you about how fast the space is growing?
turns.zh: 就像 David 说的，主动 ETF 已经成为 ETF 行业里增长最快的板块之一。发行在加速，数量上甚至已经超过了被动产品。但在我们谈谁在买之前，BNY 的数据能告诉你这个领域增长得有多快吗？

turns.en: Yeah, again, thanks. Great question, Sharun. I think, look, the data is clear. We have seen the growth of active ETFs really across the spectrum. And while we're focused here on the U.S., it's actually a global phenomenon that is starting to happen. So when you look at the data, it's quite compelling. And again, there's lots of statistics out there. We see what's happening at the industry where really the size, which is around 12 plus percent of the AUM of the industry, is running about three times its weight because the flows have been roughly three times as high. And we've seen that number continue to pick up. What is notable also is that this is not only an equity story. Certainly fixed income has picked up quite a bit as well when you look at the industry data. But when you look at BNY's own data, what we can see from our own clients is, well, about the same, right? And when we look at our active ETF that are on our platform, we see an increase of about 56% over last year in terms of the active ETF flows that we see coming through our clients. And honestly, it's the same really across the spectrum in terms of equities, but also fixed income. There are obviously some variables, but we see that acceleration in the growth. You know, also we do see that, of course, the money is also going into core building blocks. So as the old saying goes, passive is still massive. So we are seeing growth. We are seeing plenty of growth there. And again, you see that in the record industry statistics, but also It really is those, but the active ETFs is what's really notable. And there are a few categories that have really picked up. And I think a lot of that also has to do with markets. The other thing that I think is really important to understand and maybe a topic to probe is that when we do look at the data, the other notable feature here is the breadth of what we see. So, you know, this is not just a handful of ETFs. I think there was a recent stat that I saw that was more than 90% of the active ETFs have taken in money, largely what we are seeing on our own platform. And so we've seen the concentration in active ETFs on our platform begin to reduce in terms of the haves versus the have-nots. And so a bigger piece of the story is the breadth. And we see that money going to multiple tickers, multiple managers, and again, multiple investment types across the board. So it really has changed quite a bit in the last couple of years.
turns.zh: 嗯，还是要谢谢。好问题，Sharun。我觉得，看，数据是很清楚的。我们看到主动 ETF 的增长其实是全方位的。虽然这里我们聚焦的是美国，但它实际上是一个正在发生的全球现象。所以你看数据的话，是相当有说服力的。市面上的统计很多。我们看到行业层面的情况是：主动 ETF 的规模大约占行业管理资产（AUM）的 12% 以上，但资金流占比大约是它权重的三倍，因为这个领域的流入大致高出三倍。而且我们看到这个数字还在继续上升。同样值得注意的是，这不只是一个股票的故事。看行业数据，固定收益显然也涨了不少。但看 BNY 自己的数据，我们从自己客户身上看到的，基本也差不多，对吧？当我们看自己平台上托管的主动 ETF 时，从客户那里流过来的主动 ETF 资金比去年同期增长了大约 56%。说实话，各个类型基本都一样，股票是这样，固定收益也是这样。当然会有一些变量差异，但我们确实看到了增长的加速。另外我们当然也看到，钱同样在流向核心的组合基石（core building blocks）。所以就像那句老话说的，被动依然巨大（passive is still massive）。所以我们看到增长，那边也有大量增长。你在创纪录的行业统计数字里能看到这一点，但真正值得关注的还是主动 ETF。有几个品类确实起飞了，我觉得这在很大程度上也和市场有关。另一件我认为很重要、也许值得深挖的事情是：当我们看数据时，另一个显著特征是广度（breadth）。所以你知道，这不只是少数几只 ETF。我记得最近看到一个统计，说超过 90% 的主动 ETF 都拿到了资金流入，这和我们在自己平台上看到的情况大体一致。所以我们平台上主动 ETF 的集中度——就是「有钱的」和「没钱的」之间的分化——开始下降了。因此这个故事里更大的一块是广度。我们看到资金流向多只代码、多家管理人，以及多种投资类型，全面铺开。所以过去几年这个领域确实变化很大。

turns.en: When you break down that growth, I mean, you mentioned both equity and fixed income and, you know, it is kind of spread out. Are you seeing it, I guess, when we get down to the strategy level in terms of like security selection and then kind of what we call new active, you know, the different types of new products, whether it's option and stuff is, Is the growth being driven by a range of different strategies or is there kind of a group of categories that are kind of leading this?
turns.zh: 当你拆解这个增长的时候——我是说，你提到了股票和固定收益，而且它确实比较分散。落到策略层面，比如证券选择，还有我们所说的「新主动」（new active），各种新型产品，比如期权类的东西——这个增长是由一系列不同策略共同驱动的，还是说有某一组品类在领跑？

turns.en: Yeah, it's the old, I think you're asking the old question, like what does active mean to you? And this is sometimes not always something that everyone can agree on. So I'll take the high road here. I'm not gonna try to define it, but I'm gonna do my best to answer your question, okay? So when we look at our data again, largely the same as what we are seeing across the industry. No real change. What is interesting, again, is on our platform, we are seeing a higher adoption rate than the industry, not by a large margin, but a higher adoption rate at BNY Persian, for example, than the industry as a whole for active ETFs. But what is notable is that, like, where is that money coming from, which is your question. So the way I like to think about it is really sort of really high active share or active discretionary, concentrated, active, sometimes I like to call it active active, whatever you want to call it, that is taking a good chunk of the flow that we see. So roughly two thirds of that flow is actually going into that bucket of that sort of higher active share or true active product. And a higher percentage is actually in the fixed income bucket. So when you break those between equities and fixed income, actually there's more, more, a higher percentage of fixed income in that category than when you look at equities. Then again, there's a lot of terms to describe it, but I'm going to call it rules-based active or systematic active. we can even go so far as smart beta, if you will. But I won't go there. I'll just say rules-based, quantitatively driven active product. You know, that is another, obviously, another large category, roughly 30% or so of that active flow is going into a category that we can loosely define as that systematic active. And I think Many of the types of managers that listeners will be familiar with that fall into that category that have been sort of leaders in that space are contained in that category. So these are issuers like Dimensional, these Avantis, JP Morgan, Fidelity, and so on have these types of products and those loosely fall under that category. Much higher tilt there towards equities, much more of a nascent category in the fixed income space. Then we have this big other bucket, which is hard to define. But a lot of that, the balance of the actively managed products that we see, I'll say loosely fall under that thematic sort of moniker that are really designed to provide some kind of exposure to a theme, but are not necessarily tied to a particular benchmark, hence the active, properly tagged as active for investors. That category is actually sort of between those three that I just mentioned is actually the smallest, but actually receives probably an outsized amount of attention and has actually been the fastest growing category. And we've seen some real hits in some of the products, despite being a relatively small portion of the overall assets. And of course, as many of your listeners would know, And all of us hanging around the ETF space know a lot of innovation and products also coming to market there in that sort of active thematic space for sure. And we've seen that trend for at least the last couple of years, and it seems to be picking up intensity.
turns.zh: 是啊，这其实是个老问题，你问的是——主动对你来说意味着什么？这事儿大家并不总能达成一致。所以我这里走个高层路线，我不去试图定义它，但我会尽力回答你的问题，好吗？再看我们的数据，和行业整体基本一样，没什么实质变化。有意思的是，在我们平台上，主动 ETF 的采用率比行业更高——不是高很多，但比如 BNY Pershing 的采用率就高于行业整体。而值得注意的是，这些钱是从哪来的，也就是你问的问题。我喜欢这么想：真正高主动份额（high active share）的、主动决策型的、集中的主动产品——我有时候喜欢叫它「主动中的主动」（active active），随你怎么叫——拿走了我们看到资金流中的一大块。大致三分之二的资金流实际上进了这个桶，也就是那种更高主动份额、真正主动的产品。而且固定收益在这个桶里的占比更高。所以当你把股票和固定收益拆开看，固定收益落在这个类别里的比例其实比股票更高。然后——描述它的词很多——我把它叫作规则驱动的主动（rules-based active）或者系统化主动（systematic active），甚至可以叫 smart beta，但我就不往那儿说了。我就说是规则化、量化驱动的主动产品。这显然又是另一个大类别，大约 30% 左右的主动资金流进了这个可以宽松定义为系统化主动的类别。我想很多听众熟悉的、属于这个类别并且一直是该领域领头羊的管理人类型，都包含在这个桶里。比如说 Dimensional、Avantis、JP Morgan、Fidelity 等等这些发行人都有这类产品，大致都归到这个类别。这一类明显更偏向股票，在固定收益领域还只是个新生品类。然后我们还有另一个大桶，很难定义。剩下那部分主动管理产品，我会宽松地归到「主题型」（thematic）这个名头下面——它们其实是设计来提供某种主题敞口的，但不一定绑定某个特定基准，所以才叫主动，对投资者来说也是恰当地被标为主动。这个类别，在我刚说的三者之间其实是规模最小的，但受到的关注可能超出其体量，而且是增长最快的类别。我们看到有些产品成了真正的爆款，尽管它在整体资产里占比相对小。当然，正如你们很多听众知道、所有在 ETF 圈里混的人都知道，那个主动主题的空间里也有大量创新产品在上市。这个趋势我们已经看到至少两年了，而且似乎还在加强。

turns.en: Ben, something that we're really interested in getting to know is who is actually driving the buying here? One of the advantages of BNY's platform is you can look beneath the aggregate flows numbers that we typically can see. Could you tell us more about the parties that are driving the active ETF boom? Is it RIAs, wire house advisors, centralized models, or some combination of those parties?
turns.zh: Ben，我们特别想了解的一点是，到底是谁在推动这里的买入？BNY 平台的一个优势是，你能看到我们通常只能看到的总量资金流数字下面的东西。你能多讲讲推动这轮主动 ETF 繁荣的是哪些参与方吗？是 RIA（注册投资顾问）、wire house 的顾问、集中化模型（centralized models），还是这几方的某种组合？

turns.en: Yeah, it's absolutely a combination. When you look at the data, so all the signals there are green when you look at it across channel. There's a lot to unpack there, but I'll try to give a little context for what's been happening really in the last you know, at least this year or in the last several quarters. Certainly, the wire houses, especially rep as PM programs and the IRA, the RIAs rather, are early adopters. So we all kind of know that. And now what we're seeing is the, many of the independent BDs are starting to catch up and we're seeing that in some of the underlying data as they become increasing users of ETFs. I think second back to our earlier question on active, very notable trend there. We are seeing that growth. And those stats that I quoted later are coming across all these channels, those independent BDs, the wires, and RIAs. And again, actually in that order, in terms of the rate of growth, but all very significant growth numbers coming through all of those channels. You know, I think what is also happening, you know, certainly we're seeing the rise of use of these products in ETF models. So when we also, you know, look at our data and do some deep dive research on it and, you know, at BNY, we're able to track that data, sort of a group called Growth Dynamics, which does really incredible work for clients trying to really unpack, you know, these trends and this type of data. And when you look at it, it is tough to get at the exact amount of those model driven assets. But based on the data that we can see, the patterns and how they trade, it is absolutely clear that actively managed products are making their way into these models. And it is no doubt going to be an increasing source of flow as one, just these platforms, the RIAs, the wires included, are becoming more comfortable adding some measure of active products. I think there are lots of reasons for that and happy to expand on it if you want to talk about that. But it is just in the end clear that it's happening and the issuers are starting to manufacture active products to fit into those models.
turns.zh: 是的，绝对是组合。看数据的话，按渠道全面来看，所有信号灯都是绿的。这里面有很多可以展开的，但我试着给一点背景，说说今年、或者说最近几个季度到底在发生什么。当然，wire house（大型券商财富管理平台），尤其是 rep-as-PM 项目，以及 RIA，是早期采用者，这点我们都知道。而现在我们看到的是，很多独立经纪商（independent BD）开始赶上来了，我们在一些底层数据里能看到这一点，他们越来越多地使用 ETF。第二，回到我们刚才关于「主动」的问题，那里有个非常值得注意的趋势。我们看到那种增长，而我后面引用的那些统计数据，是横跨所有这些渠道出现的——独立经纪商、wire house 和 RIA。而且按增长速度排序，其实就是这个顺序，所有这些渠道都有非常可观的增长数字。我觉得另一件正在发生的事情是，我们确实看到这些产品在 ETF 模型（models）中的使用在上升。所以当我们看自己的数据、做一些深入研究时——在 BNY，我们有一个叫 Growth Dynamics 的团队能追踪这些数据，他们为客户做的工作非常出色，真的在努力拆解这些趋势和这类数据。你看下来，要精确算出这些模型驱动资产的规模是挺难的。但根据我们能看到的数据、它们的模式和交易方式，非常清楚的是：主动管理型产品正在进入这些模型。而且毫无疑问，它会成为一个越来越大的资金流来源。一方面是因为这些平台，包括 RIA 和 wire house，越来越愿意在组合中加入一定比例的主动产品。我觉得原因有很多，如果你们想聊我可以展开。但归根结底很清楚：这件事正在发生，发行人也开始生产适配这些模型的主动产品了。

turns.en: More just on the buyer mix, how has that buyer mix changed over the last few years? Are there channels that were relatively small users of active ETFs in the past that are becoming much more important?
turns.zh: 再多问一句买方结构（buyer mix）：过去几年这个买方结构有什么变化吗？有没有一些渠道过去是主动 ETF 的相对小众使用者，现在却变得越来越重要？

turns.en: I mean, I don't necessarily think the buyer mix has changed dramatically. I would sort of just think it's more of like an acceleration of adoption. And I believe that there are several reasons for this. Hard to pinpoint it exactly. But what I would say is if you look back at all of the product launches, so I mean, Bloomberg does an incredible job tracking all of, the product launches, the ETF product launches that are coming to market. It's not easy to do given the volume that we're seeing. So I get it. But at the same time, what you've seen over the last few years is that many of these metal, but many of these products have begun to scale. Many of these products have also built their multi-year track records. And so that and also have trading volume as well. So another piece, feature of ETFs. But ultimately, many of those factors or those factors have been a catalyst to help increase adoption because it has made those products more eligible for either larger institution allocations, model placement, and generally approval on the platforms. So if we were talking, maybe even 18 months ago, not that long, a couple of years ago, which is light years in ETF time, I'd be having a little bit of a different story and sort of citing what I just said as to some degree, an impediment to adoption. But now we see that really starting to change. And obviously I'm making a general statement. There's so many products that have been launched in 2026. They're not all, not every product is scaled or has those track records, but It is very clear that over the last three to five years that those products have really, you know, there is a much larger selection of choice between product and issuer and just product type that have those attributes. And so it's sort of creating this flywheel effect that is helping to really grow across channels. And they've been adopting at different rates, but everything's in the green as the data shows.
turns.zh: 我是说，我并不觉得买方结构发生了剧烈变化。我更愿意把它看成采用速度的加快。我相信这背后有好几个原因，很难精确指出到底是哪个。但我会说，如果你回头看所有的产品发行——我是说，Bloomberg 在追踪所有 ETF 产品发行方面做得非常出色，考虑到我们看到的发行量，这并不容易，所以我理解。但与此同时，过去几年你看到的是，这些产品中的许多——不是全部，但很多——已经开始形成规模，很多也已经建立了多年的业绩记录（track record），还有了成交量，这也是 ETF 的另一个特征。最终，这些因素成了推动采用率提升的催化剂，因为它们让这些产品更有资格获得大型机构的配置、进入模型，以及在平台上获得普遍审批。所以如果我们是在大概 18 个月前聊天——那也不算很久，几年前，在 ETF 的时间尺度上那是光年——我讲的故事会有点不一样，会把我刚说的那些东西在某种程度上当作采用的障碍来引用。但现在我们看到情况真的开始变了。当然我说的是一个总体判断。2026 年发行了非常多的产品，它们并非都已经形成规模或有那些业绩记录，但非常清楚的是，在过去三到五年里，具备这些属性的产品，无论从产品、发行人还是产品类型来看，可选择面都大了很多。这就形成了一种飞轮效应（flywheel effect），帮助各渠道真正增长。它们的采用速度各不相同，但就像数据显示的，所有指标都是绿的。

turns.en: Are you seeing differences in the behavior of the advisors, whether it's an IAR at an RAA firm or a wire house advisor in the way they're using active ETFs? Or is it kind of similar, you think?
turns.zh: 你有没有看到顾问行为上的差异——不管是 RIA 公司的 IAR（投资顾问代表）还是 wire house 的顾问——在使用主动 ETF 的方式上？还是说你觉得差不多？

turns.en: Yeah, it's really interesting. I think it's really been hand-to-hand combat there. So I think it's hard to, I would say it's hard to generalize. And it's funny for me to say that because I just generalized and gave you some interesting stats that I'm seeing across the industry. But I will just say, yes, there is certainly some difference in behavior in the data that we do see. Obviously, when we talk about RIA channel specifically, Historically, as I mentioned earlier, we have seen them as early adopters, certainly of ETFs. So some of the data would indicate that we've seen more of that pattern play out in the RIA channel or independent advisors being a little more friendly to using active fixed income ETFs inside their portfolio. So I think That's sort of interesting. I think it's part of that quote unquote early adopter trend. Also, again, there's more products available. But also part of that is just simply market driven. As we know, we've seen obviously a shift in the yield curve, certainly in 2026, which has really helped to kind of fuel the interest in part to these products. On the other side, I think we have seen an uptick when you look at some of the wire house channel as an example, compared to RIAs and like the clients, for example, many of the clients that use BNY Pershing or our wealth solutions platform have also changed a bit where the data also seems to show that they are using more again of those actively managed ETFs inside models. Notable big opportunity for the ETF issuers. Second, we are seeing just because of the sheer demand and what's happening in the market, we have seen more of the thematic ETFs clearly creep in to the wire house channel. And so these obviously are the major broker-dealer platforms that we all know. I wouldn't say it's in mass. And what I just said doesn't apply to all products, but there have been several hot themes that certainly have you know begun to grow and we've seen an uptick uh in the use of the products but also back to my comment earlier it also is part of that breadth story where you know historically there was always one or two sort of hot themes and you would see that in the data but we're starting to see that sort of widen out and it is quite clear uh in the data that that we see.
turns.zh: 是的，这真的很有意思。我觉得那里基本上是近身肉搏战。所以我觉得很难一概而论。我说这话有点好笑，因为我刚刚就做了个概括，还给你们讲了一些我在行业里看到的有意思的数据。但我会说，是的，在我们看到的数据里，行为上确实存在一些差异。显然，具体说到 RIA 渠道，历史上——就像我前面提到的——我们把他们看作早期采用者，至少对 ETF 是这样。所以有些数据显示，那种模式更多是在 RIA 渠道上演，也就是独立顾问更愿意在组合里使用主动固定收益 ETF。我觉得这挺有意思的。我认为这是那个所谓「早期采用者」趋势的一部分。另外，可获得的产品也更多了。但其中一部分也纯粹是市场驱动的。我们知道，收益率曲线显然在 2026 年发生了转变，这在很大程度上助推了对这类产品的兴趣。另一方面，如果你看 wire house 渠道，和 RIA 相比，我们看到有所上升。比如使用 BNY Pershing 或我们财富解决方案平台的很多客户，情况也有了些变化——数据似乎同样显示，他们在模型里使用了更多主动管理型 ETF。这对 ETF 发行人来说是个显著的大机会。第二，正因为需求量太大、市场上正在发生这些事，我们看到更多主题 ETF 明显渗入了 wire house 渠道。这些当然就是我们都知道的那些大型经纪商平台。我不会说这是普遍现象，我刚才讲的也不适用于所有产品，但确实有几个热门主题开始增长，我们看到这些产品的使用在上升。而且回到我前面的评论，这也是「广度」故事的一部分：历史上总会有一两个热门主题，你在数据里能看到；但我们开始看到这个范围在扩大，在我们看到的数据里这一点相当清楚。

turns.en: Ben, how much growth is coming from an advisor selecting an individual active ETF themselves versus it just being incorporated into a centralized or third-party model portfolio?
turns.zh: Ben，有多少增长来自顾问自己挑选某一只主动 ETF，又有多少其实是它被纳入了集中化的或第三方的模型组合？

turns.en: Yeah, I mean, look, it's changing. Obviously, I'll just say that, again, in our experience, the home office, I mean, the whole business is shifting. Probably a fun topic for another podcast or you guys are probably covering it for sure. But that whole business is really changing. And, you know, it's been, you know, obviously quite disruptive. One of the myriad of things that are happening, you know, as a result of sort of the shifts in the business has been really the centralization of some of that decision making and into the home office as sort of the role of the advisor has changed. And again, you've seen that bear out in the data. We all see that happening. And again, it just goes back to the importance of the availability of ETFs in models, their use, and that being a larger and larger driver of flow and I think to me that that is really the key thing for ETFs. I think given the changes in the landscape and sort of the role of the advisor, the technology shifting around the industry that is really causing some and will cause obviously changes going forward. will continue to have different impacts. But when it comes to ETFs today, that that trend that has been in place for a while seems to be picking up steam. So more and more of what we can see is coming through, um, you know, again, or driven by those, those home office, those models, um, and less and less in the hands of the, advisor who is doing the stock or bond selection and using ETFs to express those views directly.
turns.zh: 是啊，我是说，看，情况在变化。显然我只能说，同样以我们的经验，总部（home office）——我是说整个业务都在转变。这可能是另一档播客的有趣话题，或者你们肯定也在报道。但那整个业务确实在变，而且显然相当具有颠覆性。作为业务转变带来的众多变化之一，就是随着顾问角色的改变，一部分决策权被集中到了总部。这一点你在数据里也能看到印证，我们都能看到它正在发生。而这又回到了 ETF 在模型中的可得性、它们的使用，以及这成为越来越大的资金流驱动力这件事的重要性上。对我来说，这才是 ETF 真正关键的东西。考虑到行业格局的变化、顾问角色的变化，以及行业周边正在发生、显然还将继续引发变化的技术变革，这些会带来不同的影响。但就今天的 ETF 而言，那个已经存在了一段时间的趋势似乎在加速。所以我们能看到的越来越多的资金，是由那些总部、那些模型驱动的，而越来越少地掌握在亲自做股票或债券选择、并用 ETF 直接表达这些观点的顾问手里。

turns.en: I mean, definitely frees up time for the advisor. Interesting to watch what happens with that. But you kind of alluded to this earlier in terms of some advisors picking active fixed income ETFs. And so I was just curious if you're seeing differences of who's buying the active equity ETFs versus who is buying the active fixed income ETFs.
turns.zh: 我是说，这确实给顾问腾出了时间。看着这个变化会怎么发展很有意思。但你前面有点提到了某些顾问在挑主动固定收益 ETF。所以我好奇，你有没有看到买主动股票 ETF 的人和买主动固定收益 ETF 的人之间的差异。

turns.en: Yeah. It's, you mean like the, the, you mean like the, the type, the, like the profile of, are you talking about really more like the profile of the advisor or? Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯，这个……你是指那个类型，就是……画像（profile）？你其实更多是在说顾问的画像吗？还是？嗯。

turns.en: Well, whether it's, you know, the type of advisor, you know, whether they're part of a warehouse or if they're independent or, you know, I guess, or the type of, you know, a different type of advisor, you know, the, I guess like their, um, their clientele. I'm not sure if you can see that though.
turns.zh: 呃，就是顾问的类型，比如说他们是隶属于 wire house 还是独立的，或者……我想是不同类型的顾问，或者说他们的客户群体（clientele）。不过我不确定你们能不能看到那一层数据。

turns.en: Yeah. You know, it's, it's interesting. Um, Really, you know, it's tough to get at that individual data. Again, there are some, given what we are able to see, we do have somewhat of a lens there. I think, you know, I think part of it also that we didn't really mention is that we do see a structural shift, obviously, as we know, happening. So we do see and continue to see money that is coming out of mutual funds into ETFs, of course. And it's almost been like a seesaw type of chart or sort of approach with that money coming out and into ETFs. We see that really across the board. So that is one piece of sort of the behavior that we continue to see. I think So what's also notable, again, is that we've seen that across channel, of course, at what seems to be sort of similar rates across the board. And I think, second, I do think that we have seen maybe what is, again, more notable and kind of the topic here, again, back to active ETFs, we haven't really talked much about passive, but ultimately huge part of the ETF story. But we are seeing several of the, again, the types of clients that we see, and certainly some of those larger RIAs and larger wire house teams, again, also become more aggressive adopters of ETFs. Again, I think it goes back to what we were talking about before. The data, again, shows that type of growth where you're kind of seeing these bigger teams, again, to some degree, shed some of the individual stock and bond picking and now are going to leverage ETFs for that use. That comment really is around not just active ETFs, but really across the board. So I think the the use cases shifting. We've also seen, I think, another piece that has been covered in a big area of the growth that I also didn't cover was really around what's happening in the option ETF space. And so these are actually more structured product replacements. Very difficult to see the data to know exactly what is shifting. But the growth in that space is absolutely clear. And we have seen meaningful growth across the board in those kind of products. And a good chunk of those products are coming direct, or excuse me, the flow is not just retail flow, but it's coming through those financial advisors. So it is also another potential source or shift in the use case that we're seeing for ETFs really across channel.
turns.zh: 是啊，你知道，这挺有意思的。呃，真的，要拿到那种个体层面的数据挺难的。不过基于我们能看到的东西，我们确实有一个观察的视角。我觉得还有一部分我们其实没提到的是：我们确实看到了一个结构性的转变在发生，这我们都知道。所以我们看到、并且持续看到资金从共同基金流向 ETF。这几乎就像一个跷跷板式的图表或者说走势，钱从那边出来、进到 ETF 里。我们看到这在各类产品上都是如此。这是我们持续看到的行为中的一块。我觉得同样值得注意的是，这一点在各渠道都能看到，而且看起来速度大体相近。第二，我确实认为我们看到了一个更值得注意的现象，也就是这里的话题——回到主动 ETF。我们其实没怎么谈被动，但它归根结底是 ETF 故事里巨大的一部分。我们看到我们服务的几类客户，尤其是那些规模较大的 RIA 和较大的 wire house 团队，也成了 ETF 更激进的采用者。我觉得这又回到我们前面聊的：数据显示的就是那种增长，你会看到这些更大的团队在某种程度上放弃了个股和个券的挑选，转而用 ETF 来实现这个用途。这个说法其实不只是针对主动 ETF，而是全类型的。所以我觉得使用场景（use case）在转变。另外我还看到一块，是增长中一个被广泛报道、但我刚才也没覆盖的大领域，就是期权 ETF（option ETF）空间里正在发生的事。这些其实更多是结构化产品（structured product）的替代品。要看清数据、知道到底什么在转移是非常困难的，但那个领域的增长是绝对清晰的，我们看到那类产品在各个方向上都有可观增长。而且这些产品有相当大一块是直接来的，抱歉，我是说资金流不只是零售资金流，而是通过那些理财顾问过来的。所以这也是 ETF 使用场景在各渠道上正在出现或转变的另一个潜在来源。

turns.en: So Ben, you've given us a lot of insight on who the parties are that are driving this buying, but we'd like to know what are they actually buying? So when you break down active ETF flows, how much of it is going to your traditional stock and bond selection strategies versus the products you've mentioned here, such as options income, defined outcome, or systemic strategies, or other strategies of all those types?
turns.zh: 所以 Ben，你给我们讲了很多关于是哪些参与方在推动买入的洞见，但我们想知道他们到底在买什么。所以当你拆解主动 ETF 的资金流时，有多少是流向传统的股票和债券选股策略，又有多少流向你在这里提到的那些产品，比如期权收益、定义结果型（defined outcome）、系统化策略，或者其他各种类型的策略？

turns.en: Yeah. You mean like just more of like that, again, back to that sort of stock or bond, you're thinking about really more of that stock or bond picking versus sort of those other types of products, like the more systemic products?
turns.zh: 嗯。你是说，还是回到那个股票或债券的话题，你想的其实更多是那种选股选债，相对于其他类型的产品，比如更系统化的那些产品？

turns.en: Right.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: Exactly.
turns.zh: 没错。

turns.en: Just your traditional products versus, you know, the variety of products that you're seeing today.
turns.zh: 就是你们传统的那类产品，相对于你今天看到的这些五花八门的产品。

turns.en: Yeah. I mean, really the outlier probably is more bonds on that particular. So our own data that we can see You know, when we look at BNY clients right now, about 96% of the active ETF flow is going to what we'll call sort of discretionary managers on the fixed income side.
turns.zh: 嗯。我是说，真正的例外可能更多是在债券那一端。所以从我们自己能看到的数据来说——当我们现在看 BNY 的客户时，大约 96% 的主动 ETF 资金流，在固定收益这一端流向了我们可以称之为主动决策型管理人（discretionary managers）的产品。

turns.en: Right.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: So this is, you know, again, we're designed alpha fixed income strategies designed to deliver alpha versus some other, again, one of those other categories, like more quantitative rules based or some other categories. So that's, that's quite, quite notable. And then in equity, it's much lower. So in the data that we see, it's about half and half. So that's a stark contrast into what we're seeing in the fixed income side. So again, that's half going to or close to half going to that systemic or that rules-based strategy versus more of the active stock selection, higher active share or alpha targeted type of strategy. And again, we already sort of treaded on some shaky ground trying to define it all. So I'll pause again there. But the point is clear, right? So you have a stark contrast between those two. I think what may change one of the catalysts that may change those flows is the possibility or the advent of share classes. We'll see. But opening up that gateway to accelerate those flows, well, actually for fixed income, but most likely for equities primarily, will or could start to change the numbers. So I think that it's just too early at this point to really see or quote a pattern just because there's so few funds that have or share classes that have been launched to date. But it'll be really interesting to have that chat a year later and see if that starts to tilt the the data in any way and try to parse, you know, where's that fresh cash versus just the show class conversions.
turns.zh: 这就是——你知道，我们说的是追求 alpha（超额收益）的固定收益策略，设计目标是相对于其他类别——比如更量化的规则型或者其他类别——创造 alpha。所以这一点非常值得注意。而在股票端，这个比例就低得多。在我们看到的数据里，大致是一半一半。所以和固定收益端形成了鲜明对比。也就是说，大约一半、接近一半的资金流向了系统化或规则型策略，相对于更偏主动选股、更高主动份额或以 alpha 为目标的策略。而且我们前面在试图定义这一切时已经踩在有点摇晃的地面上了，所以我这里就再打住。但重点很清楚，对吧？所以这两者之间形成了鲜明对比。我觉得可能会改变这些资金流的催化剂之一，是份额类别（share classes）出现的可能性或者说问世。我们拭目以待。但打开那扇门去加速这些资金流——对固定收益来说会，但最可能主要是对股票来说——将会或者可能开始改变这些数字。所以我觉得现在下判断还太早，没法真正看出或者引用某种模式，因为到目前为止发行的带份额类别的基金还太少。但一年后再来聊这个话题会非常有意思，看看它是否开始让数据朝某个方向倾斜，并且试着分辨哪些是新增资金、哪些只是份额类别的转换。

turns.en: You had mentioned earlier that obviously there's still a ton of passive money in, you know, especially in core allocations. And so we kind of look at what's happening with active ETFs. Can you see how advisors are using them in the portfolio? Are they kind of replacing some of that passive or is it kind of more like around the edges?
turns.zh: 你前面提到过，显然还有海量的被动资金，尤其是在核心配置里。所以我们看主动 ETF 正在发生什么的时候——你能看出顾问在组合里是怎么用它们的吗？它们是在替代一部分被动，还是更多是在组合的边缘（around the edges）？

turns.en: Both. So, you know, probably not the answer you're looking for, but honestly, it's both because there's not a, I think really, again, we're seeing a little bit of both. So I think on the, you know, on the sort of replacement sort of side of it, yeah, it's been happening for a while. I think it's what is most important. And when you get out in the field and, you know, or you talk to ETF issuers, you know, generally they will, they're all some degree varying degrees of optimistic about trying to sell their active etf and maybe peel off a piece of that passive um uh the passive port of that portfolio that said it's tricky because first your those managers and i think very important for etfs are judged on their at after tax after fee performance so you know ultimately you have to be able to show value there and value for the fees that you're charging. So certainly fees obviously matter. On average, again, depending on the type of product, they're going to typically be some measure of additional fee beyond the passive, whatever the underlying passive benchmark is, of course. But the problem comes in when you see in these asset allocation models, when you're looking for the active replacement for passive, there is a real fee discussion. So you make the case that this is better and I'm going to deliver value for after fee, after tax performance. But at the same time, you know, you're ultimately, these advisors are ultimately targeting a fee. So the question is, you know, what do I need to sell or how do I need to reposition my portfolio to, basically make this allocation? And that sometimes can be a challenging question for the advisor and also even for the issuer that really does have a strong product to bring to market. And then on the edges, so back to my both argument or both answer, again, we kind of touched on it a little bit earlier, but The data shows that, yes, they are using more of these products on the edge. Lots of examples to point to. Some are, I'll say, more mundane where they're going to add a little, probably as your colleague Eric would say, a little hot sauce to the portfolio to capture a theme, you know, like semiconductor stocks, you know, the hot topic earlier this year, you know, those kinds of things to provide a portfolio tilt. or potentially leverage or short products, potentially the hedge, less frequent than what we see given our client base. That's more of a retail story, generally speaking, but again, it does appear. But then also we are seeing those other types of products to get simply access to, again, early days, but those alternative types of strategies we've seen pop up, certainly in some of the, again, on the edges. And then another story, which has been well covered for the last couple of years, our old friend digital assets, another sort of small, well, actually it's grown, but one of the use cases that we have seen in the grand scheme, small in the grand scheme of things, but certainly something we see in the data where, again, some of those assets have been brought into ETFs from wherever they were outside, most likely outside of a wrapped financial product and they had their own exposure to the digital asset have come into that ETF wrapper. And so again, another sort of simple to understand or simple to digest example of where you can see things popping up on the edges. So really strong data for both. And, you know, again, sort of back to the story that we see all things growing across the board.
turns.zh: 两者都有。所以，这大概不是你想要的答案，但老实说就是两者都有，因为并没有一个……我觉得，我们确实两种都看到一点。所以在「替代」这一边，是的，这件事已经发生一段时间了。我觉得最重要的是——当你走出去做实地调研，或者你和 ETF 发行人聊，通常他们都会以不同程度的乐观想去推销自己的主动 ETF，也许能从组合的被动那一块里切下一片。话虽如此，这事儿很棘手，因为首先，那些管理人——我觉得这对 ETF 非常重要——是要按税后、费后业绩（after tax, after fee performance）来评判的。所以你最终必须能在那里证明价值，证明相对于你收取的费用是有价值的。所以费用当然重要。平均而言，取决于产品类型，通常都会在底层被动基准之上多出一定程度的费用，这是当然的。但问题出在这里：当你在这些资产配置模型中，寻找主动来替代被动时，会有一场真正的费用讨论。你要论证这个更好，我要在费后、税后业绩上创造价值。但与此同时，这些顾问最终是有一个目标费率的。所以问题是，我需要卖什么，或者我需要怎么重新调整组合，才能基本上做出这个配置？这对顾问来说有时是个很有挑战性的问题，对那个确实有强产品要推向市场的发行人来说也是如此。然后在「边缘」这一边，回到我「两者都有」的论点或者答案——我们前面也稍微提到了——数据显示，是的，他们在边缘使用了更多这类产品。可以举的例子很多。有些我会说比较平常，比如他们会加一点——大概就像你同事 Eric 会说的那样——给组合加一点「辣酱」（hot sauce），去捕捉一个主题，比如半导体股票，年初的热门话题，那些东西，来给组合一个倾斜；或者是潜在的杠杆或做空产品，可能还有对冲——考虑到我们的客户基础，这类比我们看到的要少见，那更多是零售端的故事，一般说来是这样，但它确实会出现。然后我们也看到另外那些类型的产品，就是单纯用来获取敞口的——同样还处在早期——但那些另类策略（alternative）确实冒出来了，当然是在组合的边缘。然后还有一个故事，过去两年被广泛报道，就是我们的老朋友数字资产（digital assets）。这是另一个用例，规模在整体格局里算小的——好吧其实它已经长大了——但确实是我们从数据里看到的一个用例：其中一些资产从别的地方被搬进了 ETF，之前很可能是在某个有包装的金融产品之外，他们自己持有数字资产的敞口，现在进到了 ETF 这个外壳里。所以又是一个容易理解、容易消化的例子，说明你能在边缘看到东西冒出来。所以两边都有很强的数据支撑。而且，同样回到我们看到的故事：所有东西都在全面增长。

turns.en: That makes sense. I actually just recently put out a note just looking at, you know, how many ETFs, I mean, with so many launches, how many are actually gaining traction? And so just curious, you know, if you can see or what the NY's data can tell you about the characteristics of the funds that seem to be gaining traction, because there are a lot of launches, but not all the funds are seeing tons of assets and flows right away.
turns.zh: 这说得通。我其实最近刚发了一份报告，就是看在这么多发行的情况下，到底有多少 ETF 真正获得了牵引力（traction）。所以我很好奇，你能不能看到，或者说 BNY 的数据能告诉你，那些看起来正在获得牵引力的基金有什么特征，因为发行很多，但并不是所有基金都能马上拿到大量资产和资金流。

turns.en: Yeah. Um, I think, um, you know, again, time will tell, um, honestly, um, I've, I've, I do think it is hard to keep track. Um, and I, I, I I'll commend you again for, for doing a great job at trying to keep track of all of those, uh, new products, but I can't even imagine what it is like at this point. Um, you know, being on the other side of it as an advisor, um, you know, as a, as a, as a, you know, someone who's looking after models or someone at one of the home offices trying to make sense of all of this and sort through the noise. Not an easy thing to do these days. But I do, I think you're right. And maybe where you were going was, look, as we know, one is they're not all winners. So not all of these products are going to be gigantic hits. not all of these products will survive. We have seen an uptick in closures, a little bit less so certainly on active, because again, a lot of these products also have, on average, it has a shorter lifespan, but it's something to keep an eye on as we move forward. So I do think you know, so I do think, you know, we've seen some of that, you know, I think that's just something to, you know, kind of continue to monitor. But I do think, you know, ultimately some of these products ultimately need to incubate and it's hard to know when the market turns and a particular space is going to get hot or come into vogue. So some of what we're seeing is really, and I would expected to continue some planting of seeds. And we see a lot of clients being very aggressive with product development. And being a reformed ETF product guy myself, market timing is a very difficult thing when it comes to trying to launch an ETF. It's just, you're really thinking about today, what are investors going to want probably in three to six months? and really tough thing to do. Active is a little bit different because, again, these are designed as a whole on that many of these products are designed to be buy and hold with a longer term investment horizon. So ultimately, a little bit less time sensitive, but when you veer into some of more of these narrower systemic strategies, we talked about thematic, these can be challenging, but even with those discretionary active products, very, very difficult, even if we want to do something like European equities active or something or small cap active, when that market is going to turn or turn for or against is a very difficult thing to do. So I think we'll have to look back over the next couple of years and sort of see how those fare, because it's just kind of the nature of the business.
turns.zh: 是啊。呃，我觉得，你知道，还是时间会给出答案，说实话。我确实觉得很难跟得上。我还是要再次称赞你们，在追踪所有这些新产品方面做得非常出色，但我简直无法想象现在站在另一边是什么感受——作为一名顾问，或者作为负责模型的人，或者某个总部里试图理清这一切、从噪音里筛出信号的人。这如今可不是一件容易的事。但我确实觉得你说得对。也许你想说的是，看，我们都知道，第一，它们不全是赢家。所以不是所有这些产品都会成为巨大的爆款，不是所有这些产品都能活下来。我们看到清盘（closures）在上升，主动这块少一些，同样是因为很多这类产品平均寿命更短，但这是我们往前走时需要留意的事情。所以我确实觉得，我们看到了一些这样的情况，这就是个需要持续监测的东西。但我确实认为，最终这些产品中的一些需要时间来孵化（incubate），而且很难知道市场什么时候会转向、某个特定领域什么时候会火起来或者变得流行。所以我们看到的一些东西其实是——我也预期会继续——播种。我们看到很多客户在产品开发上非常激进。作为一个「改过行」的 ETF 产品人，我可以告诉你，在发行 ETF 这件事上做市场择时（market timing）是非常难的。你真正在想的是今天：投资者大概在三个月到六个月后会想要什么？这是件非常难做的事。主动有点不一样，因为同样，这些产品整体上很多是被设计成买入并持有、投资期限更长的。所以最终时间敏感度略低一些。但当你转向那些更狭窄的系统化策略，我们说过主题型，这些可能会有挑战。不过即便是那些主动决策型产品也非常非常难——哪怕我们想做类似欧洲股票主动或者小盘主动这样的东西，那个市场什么时候会转向、朝有利还是不利的方向转，是非常难判断的。所以我觉得我们得回头去看接下来几年的表现，因为这基本上就是这个行业的本性。
